:::{#lem-arithmetic-interval}
#### The intervals of an arithmetic code

In the [arithmetic code](#def-arithmetic-code) for $n$ [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) copies of $X$,
the final slice of a message $x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ has width $\pf{x_1} \cdots \pf{x_n}$,
and the final slices of two different messages do not overlap.

:::

::: {.proof}

Each round replaces a slice of width $b - a$ by a slice of width $(b - a) \pf{x_i}$.
After $n$ rounds the width is $\pf{x_1} \cdots \pf{x_n}$.

The parts that the values of $X$ own are the slices $[F(x), F(x) + \pf{x})$,
which do not overlap,
because each starts where the one before it ends.
So the parts of one slice do not overlap either.

Let $x$ and $x'$ be two different messages,
and let $j$ be the first position where they differ.
Before round $j$,
both messages have the same slice.
At round $j$ they take different parts of it,
which do not overlap.
Later rounds keep each slice inside its own part,
so the final slices do not overlap.

:::
